How far does the four-bit mixing criterion extend?

For pairwise mixing, the four-bit criterion also holds at five bits. Six bits is the first counterexample for bit lengths of at least two. There are counterexamples at arbitrarily large bit lengths.

Five bits

Write V=𝔽25V=\mathbb F_2^5, let TT be the group of all XOR translations, and let G=⟨T,P⟩G=\langle T,P\rangle. Two observations connect the difference walk to the action of GG.

  1. The difference graph is connected exactly when GG is 2-transitive. Here 2-transitivity means that any ordered pair of distinct points can be carried to any other. The round maps PτP\tau, for τ∈T\tau\in T, generate GG because one of them is PP and multiplying by P−1P^{-1} recovers every translation. On a finite set any inverse is a positive power. Translations move freely between pairs of a given difference. Taking differences of the pair orbits therefore gives exactly the components of the difference walk.
  2. GG is primitive exactly when PP preserves no coset partition of a proper nonzero binary subspace. Primitive means there is no nontrivial partition of the points which the group permutes. In any invariant partition let WW be the part containing zero. For w∈Ww\in W, the translate w+Ww+W meets WW at ww, so it must equal WW. Thus WW is a subspace and all the parts are its cosets. Conversely, if PP permutes the cosets of WW, every generator of GG preserves that partition.

The dimension-specific input is the classification of primitive groups of degree 32. There are seven up to permutation isomorphism, and each is at least 2-transitive. Consequently a five-bit difference chain is disconnected if and only if its permutation preserves a nontrivial subspace coset partition. GAP PrimGrp coverage · Degree-32 records

For a connected difference chain of period hh, each cyclic class has the same stationary mass. Uniform is stationary, so the classes have equal size and hh divides 31. A nontrivial period is therefore 31, making every class a singleton. Every difference aa then has a deterministic successor. In symbols,

P(x+a)+P(x)=P(a)+P(0)for every x,a.P(x+a)+P(x)=P(a)+P(0)\qquad\text{for every }x,a.

This makes x↦P(x)+P(0)x\mapsto P(x)+P(0) additive, hence binary linear. Conversely, every affine map P(x)=Ax+cP(x)=Ax+c evolves differences deterministically as a↦Aaa\mapsto Aa. This proves the five-bit criterion, including periodicity.

A six-bit counterexample

Write six bits as two field elements in E=𝔽8E=\mathbb F_8. Take S(x)=x3S(x)=x^3 and

P(x,y)=(S(y),S(x)).P(x,y)=(S(y),S(x)).

Since gcd(3,7)=1\gcd(3,7)=1, SS is a permutation. For a≠0a\ne0 its derivative is

DaS(x)=(x+a)3+x3=a3(1+t+t2),t=x/a.D_aS(x)=(x+a)^3+x^3=a^3(1+t+t^2),\qquad t=x/a.

The binary linear map t↦t+t2t\mapsto t+t^2 has kernel {0,1}\{0,1\}. Hence the derivative takes four distinct values, all nonzero by injectivity of SS. In particular PP is nonaffine, and those four values span EE because a proper binary subspace of EE contains at most three nonzero vectors.

Failure of mixing. A difference (a,b)(a,b) becomes (DbS(y),DaS(x))(D_bS(y),D_aS(x)), with x,yx,y ranging independently over EE. Each output coordinate is nonzero exactly when the corresponding input difference was nonzero, with the coordinates exchanged. The number of nonzero coordinates is conserved. The 14 differences with one active coordinate can never reach the 49 with two.

Absence of a preserved coset partition. Suppose the cosets of a nonzero binary subspace WW were preserved. Then P(v+w)+P(v)∈WP(v+w)+P(v)\in W for all w∈Ww\in W and all vv. Pick a nonzero (a,b)∈W(a,b)\in W. If a≠0a\ne0, fix yy and vary xx. Adding two outputs with different second coordinates gives (0,c)∈W(0,c)\in W with c≠0c\ne0. If only b≠0b\ne0, exchange the roles of the coordinates. From (0,c)(0,c) the possible successors (DcS(y),0)(D_cS(y),0) span the first coordinate axis. Starting from any nonzero vector on that axis gives the entire second axis in the same way. Thus W=E2W=E^2.

For any k≥2k\ge2, cube each of kk three-bit blocks and cyclically rotate the blocks. The number of nonzero difference blocks is conserved, and the single-axis argument propagates around the entire cycle. More generally, any odd block length b≥3b\ge3 works over 𝔽2b\mathbb F_{2^b}. The cube is bijective because 33 is coprime to 2b−12^b-1, and each nonzero derivative takes 2b−12^{b-1} nonzero values, enough to span the block.

An exact criterion for every bit length

Let mm be the order of PP. Form the group

H=⟨PjTP−j:0≤j<m⟩.H=\langle P^j T P^{-j}:0\le j<m\rangle.

Then the pairwise difference chain mixes if and only if HH is 2-transitive. More generally, for 2≤t≤|V|2\le t\le |V|, the cipher converges to uniform on ordered distinct tt-tuples from every starting tuple if and only if HH is tt-transitive.

To prove this, group rounds into blocks of mm. Move every occurrence of PP to the right in the product of the mm round maps. The remaining factors are conjugates of translations, and PmP^m is the identity. Conversely, setting all keys to zero realizes the identity, and allowing just one key to vary realizes any translation in any one of the conjugate groups. Thus the block transitions generate exactly HH and include a self-loop. They mix uniformly on each HH-orbit because the transitions average permutations. Convergence from every start to the uniform law on all distinct tt-tuples is therefore equivalent to having a single orbit. Uniform is stationary for each individual round, so convergence along the block endpoints also gives convergence at every round. For pairs, T⊆HT\subseteq H ensures that the orbits are unions of whole difference fibers, giving the same criterion for the difference chain.

Deciding pairwise mixing from a truth table

Write N=2nN=2^n and D={1,…,N−1}D=\{1,\ldots,N-1\}. For every xx, the map Rx(a)=P(x)⊕P(x⊕a)R_x(a)=P(x)\oplus P(x\oplus a) permutes DD. The transition rule on differences is the uniform average of these permutations. Consequently the chain is doubly stochastic, uniform is stationary, and each weak component of the directed support graph is strongly connected. For the last claim, a sink component has zero flow leaving it and therefore zero flow entering it. Remove it and repeat on the other components.

Exact characterization. Failure to converge from every start is equivalent to at least one of the following conditions.

  • Some nonempty proper subset of DD contains Rx(a)R_x(a) for every member aa and every xx.
  • There is a partition into d>1d>1 nonempty classes such that every RxR_x advances the class of its argument by one modulo dd.

The first condition describes disconnection. If the graph is connected, the second is precisely periodicity. In the remaining case the finite chain is irreducible and aperiodic and its powers converge to uniform. Jarvis and Shier, Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Finite Markov Chains, section 17.3

Algorithm. Start a breadth-first search at difference 1, generating successors on demand. For each reached aa, it suffices to visit each unordered pair {x,x⊕a}\{x,x\oplus a\} once. Keep the search depth h(a)h(a) and the running gcd of the integers h(a)+1−h(b)h(a)+1-h(b) over encountered edges a→ba\to b. Tree edges contribute zero.

If the queue empties before all states are found, the reached states form a proper closed set. Otherwise the full graph is strongly connected. Its period equals that gcd. To prove this, the sum of the edge expressions around a cycle telescopes to the cycle length, so the gcd divides every cycle length. Conversely, for each edge a→ba\to b, choose any path from bb back to the root. The tree path to aa followed by this edge and the return path is a closed walk. So is the tree path to bb followed by the same return path. The period divides both lengths, hence divides their difference h(a)+1−h(b)h(a)+1-h(b).

This supplies witnesses as well as a decision. If the period d>1d>1, the classes are h(a)moddh(a)\bmod d. Once every state has been discovered and the running gcd reaches one, the decision is already mixing. Additional edges preserve reachability, and their gcd with one remains one.

There are N−1N-1 possible rows and N/2N/2 unordered pairs in each. The search uses O(N2)O(N^2) worst-case word operations and O(N)O(N) words of storage, with O(n)O(n)-bit words. A nonzero running gcd can strictly decrease only O(logN)O(\log N) times, and unchanged updates take a constant number of word remainders. This keeps the total cost quadratic. The implementation also tests affineness in one pass by inductively reconstructing the normalized linear map from its basis images. For an affine input it follows just the single successor in each reached row.

For a fixed tuple order tt, the same graph method extends by storing the t−1t-1 differences from the first input. These are ordered, distinct and nonzero, so there are M=(N−1)(N−2)⋯(N−t+1)M=(N-1)(N-2)\cdots(N-t+1) states. Each xx applies the same RxR_x to every coordinate. Scanning the transitions costs O(tNM)O(tNM) time, polynomial in the truth-table length for fixed tt. A fresh common XOR key uniformizes the first coordinate conditional on the difference tuple, giving the corresponding ordered-output guarantee one cipher round later.
